claims.statement: Without shift, RWN and the baseline had indistinguishable MAE (0.409 ± 0.007 vs 0.412 ± 0.006, 5 seeds).

Under level shifts of 0.2-0.6 training-std units, RWN reduced MAE by 11-29% relative to the baseline, with the gap growing with shift magnitude; seed spread (std ≤ 0.012) is small relative to the differences.
At shift 0.8, RWN gave no clear benefit (0.712 ± 0.021 vs 0.731 ± 0.015; difference about one standard deviation).
At shift 0.6, freezing statistics after the first post-shift window (RWN-fixed, MAE 0.518) recovers about two thirds of RWN's gain over the baseline; about one third depends on continued adaptation.
Because capacity was held fixed, the results suggest that stale normalization statistics, rather than model capacity, account for much of the baseline's shift-induced error in this setting.
confidence_reasons: capacity not varied, only held constant

claims.statement: We hypothesized that per-window normalization would reduce error under level shift without harming accuracy when no shift occurs.
Whether the effect holds on real load data and larger architectures remains open.

limitations.statement: All data come from one synthetic generator; transfer to real load series is untested.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Effect sizes may not carry over to real data.

limitations.statement: A single architecture was used and capacity was never varied; the capacity explanation was held constant, not tested.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: The 'rather than capacity' part of C005 is inferred, not isolated.

limitations.statement: The window length (48) was not tuned.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Reported gains are for one untuned setting; they may be higher or lower when tuned.
No claim about variance or seasonality shifts.
